title: Free Fries, One RULE 🍟
premise: At this diner the fries are free, forever. Two yellow gloves slide every basket out of the order hatch, nobody has seen the cook, and the one rule is never look in the kitchen. My best friend Omar and I are broke, so we sit in the same booth every day at four. My fries taste just like my mom's, her kitchen across town smells of fries though nobody's cooked, and she's asleep on the couch by five. Omar bets me his last dollar I won't look.
twist: Through the kitchen door's round window is my mom's kitchen: she fries my basket in her own yellow gloves, eyes shut, every afternoon, never knowing. Whoever cooks for you most makes your fries, so Omar and I start cooking dinner for her every night until we are the ones who cook for her most. Now the second she orders, we blink and we're at our stove holding a fry basket.
world: a small bright retro diner in afternoon sun with a mint booth, a chrome order hatch under a round glowing 0.00 sign and a kitchen door with one round window, and a yellow home kitchen across town
